Need to put up the correction post for the GST template tonight, before more people file with it. Everything is on the blog dashboard: Ravi's and Shu Fen's comments, Melvin's complaint, my working notes and the changelog. Please draft it as a new post (draft only, I will read through before publishing). Explain plainly what was wrong with the formula, who is affected and what they should do now. I want to own the mistake properly but I don't want it to read like a grovelling apology either. Keep it in my usual style. For the worked example please use Ravi's $1,090 takings, the wrong $98.10 GST and correct $90, a difference of $8.10; don't introduce other example amounts.

- wrong formula was inclusive takings x 9%; correct is 9/109 of inclusive takings. Ravi's example $1,090 day gave $98.10 instead of $90
- affected v1.0, v1.1, v1.2. Fixed v1.3 uploaded 8 Nov. 412 downloads since 12 Aug
- already filed: IRAS has its own rules on whether an error goes into a later F5 or needs a GST F7. Don't state the rules myself, point readers to the IRAS errors page and their filer
- only people entering GST-inclusive takings are hit (most hawkers). H2 must match the amounts entered: 'prices exclude GST' only for entries excluding GST; inclusive setting for receipts including GST, even if menu prices exclude it
- I tested v1.0 against my own sample figures which were already ex-GST, so the check passed. That's how I missed it
- error was mine, no excuses. But it overstates GST, so nobody underpaid IRAS. People may have overpaid and should check the correction route with IRAS or their filer
- Melvin is right to be upset, people trusted it because I'm an accountant
- thank Ravi and Shu Fen by name for catching it
- step by step for someone who already filed Q3 with the sheet
- don't name any client or my firm

(About me: accountant at a mid-size firm, 46, Singapore. Length: all the messages together should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

Things I've written before:
[The Ledger Corner (blog), 2026-10-02] If your net trade income is above $6,000 a year, you are required to make MediSave contributions. Most people know this in theory. In practice, I still see the same three mistakes every filing season.

The first is treating gross receipts as net trade income. They are not the same thing. Your Grab or delivery earnings, minus allowable expenses, is the figure that matters. If you key in the gross amount, you will be told to contribute more than you need to, and getting it reversed is a hassle.

The second is leaving it until the Notice of Computation arrives and then being surprised by the lump sum. You can pay monthly by GIRO. Do consider it, especially if your income is lumpy.

The third is assuming that because you have been employed for part of the year, your employer's CPF covers everything. It covers the employment portion only.

None of this is complicated once you see it laid out. If you are unsure, check the CPF Board's calculator before you file, not after.
[The Ledger Corner (blog), 2026-06-18] I will say it again because it bears repeating: please open a separate bank account for your stall.

I know it feels like extra admin. My late father ran a drinks stall in Toa Payoh for twenty-two years and never once had a separate account. Everything went into one POSB passbook, and at year end my mother would sit at the kitchen table with a calculator trying to work out which withdrawals were for sugar and condensed milk and which were for our school fees. I was the one who eventually took over that job, which is probably how I ended up in this line of work.

A separate account does two things. It gives you a clean record when IRAS asks questions, and it lets you see, honestly, whether the stall is making money. Many owners are surprised. Some pleasantly, some not.

It costs nothing at most banks if you keep a small balance. Do it this month, before the year-end rush, and you will thank yourself when the Notice of Assessment comes.
